cases.reason: A, B and C published signed kind-10050 inbox lists through the UI; independent relay queries verified signatures and B’s two authorized inboxes.
A and B exchanged real NIP-17 messages through Geode; both UI contexts decrypted the intended text, C received none, and relay storage contained only valid encrypted gift wraps.

A fixed rightward touch swipe selected its exact reply target; ArrowUp edited the latest eligible own message only with an empty composer; cancel preserved the draft and neither shortcut published a relay event.

Valid npub/nprofile references rendered as bounded Property cards; duplicate, invalid, nsec-looking, code-span and URL references stayed literal. Local search highlighted a profile code without flattening its card; tapping a card prefilled the existing contact dialog and relay hints without creating a conversation or publishing an event.
Conversation-list search found older locally stored direct and group messages after newer nonmatching messages, identified each chat, and opened each exact match without a relay search event.

The group composer offered local member autocomplete, Enter inserted a bound @name, NIP-27 profile references were carried inside encrypted NIP-17 content, the recipient resolved the correct member, and the relay exposed no message text.

Both Property clients rendered a local location card from the encrypted NIP-17 message. No map image or external request was made; loopback relays saw no readable coordinates or place name. The map link is explicit, uses the parsed coordinates, and its privacy notice is localized.

The forwarded NIP-17 message kept its body unchanged and showed a private “Forwarded” label to sender and recipient. The relay stored one encrypted gift wrap with neither plaintext nor the inner hop marker.
